objective: Re-assess the SubagentWorkflow renderer mitigation for whether any Pi path still evaluates a script meta fragment before the gate, and for new vulnerabilities.
scope: Previous finding to verify closed (security, pre-existing in @tintinweb/pi-subagents 0.23.1): the SubagentWorkflow renderCall (index.ts:2743) calls extractMeta (meta.ts:319, 250) and evaluates the meta fragment in vm createContext({}) during Pi interactive rendering of streamed calls (interactive-mode.js:2904-2916, 3320), before the tool_call gate, so `export const meta = { description: this.constructor.constructor(\"return process\")() }` reached the host process. The repair registers a tool renderer through pi.registerToolRenderer that replaces renderCall for SubagentWorkflow with a plain line naming the workflow only when literalWorkflowName (workflow-check.ts) vets the fragment, keeping the package renderResult and renderShell; the extension now imports @earendil-works/pi-tui at runtime. Review only d8fcbdf..HEAD in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-launcher (source diff at /home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair4.diff; package and Pi sources under /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-probe/node_modules). Do not run pi or any live model.

Trace every Pi and package path that calls renderCall, workflowCallName or extractMeta on model-supplied script text before or without the tool_call gate (streaming, history reload, session export or share, RPC or JSON event emission, the completion notice, the package widget or status line), and whether the registered resolver reliably wins (order of extension load, registration timing relative to the first render).
constraints: Read-only: no edits and no version-control writes.
Substantiate each finding with a source-to-sink path.
Start each evidence line with the criterion text, then a colon.

criteria.text: No Pi path evaluates model-supplied workflow script code on the host before the gate, and the repair adds no vulnerability

result:
result: No Pi path I could find evaluates model-supplied workflow script code before the gate, and the repair adds no vulnerability. The built-in `/security-review` could not run. I read the code only: no Bash was available, so I ran no tests or checks.

- `/security-review` via the Skill tool failed on `git diff --name-only origin/HEAD...` (`origin/HEAD` is unknown in this checkout). It covered nothing, so the review is manual and limited to d8fcbdf..HEAD (`/home/user/holyagent-notes/launcher-repair4.diff`).

notes (all non-blocking):
- **Residual bypass, documented.** An earlier-loaded resolver that returns a `SubagentWorkflow` renderer without calling `next()` would skip ours (`runner.js:542-546`). The only other resolver in Pi (mcp, `mcp/index.js:279`) calls `next()`, and the package registers none. The bypass needs another extension, which already runs arbitrary code.
- **Per-delta cost.** `workflowCallLine` parses on every streamed update with no cache or size cap. The package cached by source. The cost is linear in script size per update, plus a whitespace-backscan in `isRegexPosition`. It can only slow the UI thread, which the model can already do by emitting large output.
- **Cosmetic spoofing.** The control-character strip covers C0, DEL, C1 and U+2028/2029. Bidi overrides (U+202E) and zero-width characters stay in the shown name, and `slice(0, 80)` can split a surrogate pair.
- **Unguarded flag path.** `--subagents-workflow-file` (`index.js:2752`) calls `extractMeta` on a file the user names. The value is user-supplied, not model-supplied, so it is out of scope.

evidence:
No Pi path evaluates model-supplied workflow script code on the host before the gate, and the repair adds no vulnerability (behavior): holds.
- **Render sinks all resolve through the resolver.**
  - Pi calls `getRegisteredToolDefinition`, which calls `resolveToolRenderers`, at the streamed update (`interactive-mode.js:2908`), tool execution start (`:2979`), and history reload (`:3324`), and at `agent-session.js:3563` for HTML export and share.
  - The package's conversation viewer (`conversation-viewer.js:880`) does the same, and child sessions never get `SubagentWorkflow` (`agent-runner.ts:322`, `:1217`; `index.ts:313`).
  - The package's own `workflowCallName` has one call site, the tool's `renderCall` (`index.js:2531`), and that is the one replaced.
- **Other `extractMeta` callers are post-gate or not model-supplied.** `execute` (`index.js:2573`) runs only after the gate. The flag path is user-supplied, as noted above. `validateScript` (`runtime.js:240`) runs only in `runWorkflow`.
- **Package `renderResult`, entry renderer, widget and completion notice.** They use `task.meta` from `execute`, which is post-gate, and never read the raw script. Print and RPC modes draw nothing.
- **Registration timing.** `pi.registerToolRenderer(workflowRenderers)` (`extension.ts:723`) is synchronous in the factory. It sits outside every `pi.enable` or `held` condition and runs in children too. Pi resolves lazily at component construction, and extensions are loaded before the first render.
- **Tool name match.** The tool name is fixed and the match is exact (`index.ts:2689`). An unknown case variant has no definition and so no renderer.
- **Fallback when the tool is unregistered.** A `SubagentWorkflow` call while the tool is unregistered gets `undefined` and Pi's generic argument rendering, which evaluates nothing.
- **`literalWorkflowName`.** It reads only a vetted `ObjectExpression` of literals, parsed with acorn and never evaluated. `Effect.try` plus `Effect.catch` turns parse and stack failures into `undefined`. The `metaFragment` refactor keeps the gate's checks and `exportAt` offset unchanged.
- **pi-tui import.** Pi's loader aliases `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (`loader.js:55-75`), and it is a declared peer dependency.

acceptance.rationale: No pre-gate evaluation path remains; all render sinks go through the replaced renderer.
